page: Google Cloud Platform a3-edgegpu-8g-nolssd is an accelerator-optimized server instance designed for high-density parallel computing. It features 8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs based on the Hopper architecture, providing a total of 637 GB of VRAM. The host system is powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor with 208 vCPUs (104 physical cores) running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. System memory totals 1872.0 GB, which equates to 9.0 GB of RAM per core. This configuration does not include local SSD storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached options.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves a top-tier rating in multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and a passmark CPU score of 120,167.87. Memory bandwidth is highly rated, with uncached large-block reads reaching 423.79 GB/sec and writes at 180.61 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier capabilities in ray tracing, image processing, and LLM inference, processing 5,430.06 tokens per second for medium (7B) model prompts and generating 189.54 tokens per second. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core benchmarks falling in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the a3-edgegpu-8g-nolssd represents a high-end hardware class where the financial investment is aligned with massive parallel processing density and memory bandwidth. The primary tradeoff is the complete absence of local SSD storage, which requires relying on external storage solutions and may introduce network latency for I/O-heavy operations. It is optimized for workloads that can fully leverage the 8 H100 GPUs and high vCPU count, making it less cost-effective for tasks that rely on single-threaded performance or do not require GPU acceleration.

This server is designed for large-scale artificial intelligence and machine learning workloads, including LLM training and inference, deep learning, and complex data science jobs. It is also highly suitable for high-performance computing (HPC) tasks, ray tracing, image processing, and multi-threaded simulations that require massive parallel GPU and CPU compute capacity.
